description: 10 scenarios testing the orchestrator's ability to detect, surface, and correctly escalate or resolve conflicts between competing requirements, policies, or priorities.

scenarios.title: Urgent PO conflicts with exceeded budget
scenarios.prompt: This PO is urgent but the budget for this category is already exceeded. Process it.

expected_routing.notes: Must detect the budget conflict, surface it clearly, and escalate to exception handler — not auto-approve or auto-reject. Requires override approval from budget owner.

failure_modes: Auto-processes PO ignoring budget status
Hard-rejects PO without offering exception path
Escalates without explaining the specific conflict
scenarios.enterprise_impact: Budget overrun; audit finding; or blocked urgent purchase causing operational delay.

hitl_hotl.reason: Budget exceeded — cannot proceed without override approval from budget owner.

scenarios.title: Emergency leave requested during blackout period
scenarios.prompt: I need emergency leave immediately, but I know there's a blackout period this week.

expected_routing.notes: Blackout period + emergency leave is a legitimate conflict. Must not auto-approve (policy violation) or auto-deny (emergency). Must escalate to HR manager for judgment call.

failure_modes: Auto-approves because 'emergency' overrides all policy
Auto-denies because blackout period is active
Escalates without conveying the emergency context to the manager
scenarios.enterprise_impact: Policy violation from blanket approval; employee relations damage from blanket denial.

hitl_hotl.reason: Blackout period active — emergency leave requires HR manager sign-off before approval.

scenarios.title: VIP customer request conflicts with standard policy
scenarios.prompt: The VIP customer wants an exception to our standard return policy — they're outside the window.

expected_routing.notes: VIP status and policy exception request creates a conflict. Neither auto-grant nor auto-deny — must surface to senior CS manager with full context (VIP tier, policy rule, business value).

failure_modes: Auto-grants exception due to VIP status without escalation
Enforces standard policy ignoring VIP context
Escalates without customer tier or order details
scenarios.enterprise_impact: VIP churn from policy enforcement; or policy erosion from blanket exceptions.

hitl_hotl.reason: VIP exception request — senior CS manager has oversight window to intervene before response is sent.

scenarios.title: Urgent request conflicts with SLA constraint
scenarios.prompt: The customer is marking this as URGENT, but our SLA for this tier is 4 hours and we're at 2 hours.

expected_routing.notes: Urgency claim vs. SLA status. Must evaluate if urgency claim justifies upgrading the ticket priority (changing SLA clock) vs. explaining current SLA compliance.

failure_modes: Dismisses urgency claim because SLA clock isn't breached yet
Immediately escalates to P1 without evaluating the SLA status
Does not check whether a priority upgrade is warranted
scenarios.enterprise_impact: SLA breach if escalation delayed; customer trust erosion; contract penalty.

hitl_hotl.reason: Customer urgency claim — SLA manager has window to adjust priority before SLA clock change is committed.

scenarios.title: Regional policy conflicts with global policy
scenarios.prompt: My regional HR policy allows 30 days notice for termination, but global policy says 60 days. Which do I follow?

expected_routing.notes: Direct policy conflict — must not guess. Must surface the conflict to legal/compliance with both policy texts and escalate for authoritative ruling.

failure_modes: Applies global policy without noting the regional conflict
Applies regional policy without noting global override
Returns both policies without flagging the conflict or escalating
scenarios.enterprise_impact: Legal liability from incorrect notice period; wrongful termination claim.

hitl_hotl.reason: Policy conflict with legal implications — authoritative ruling needed before action.

scenarios.title: Multiple valid answers — select best fit for constraints
scenarios.prompt: If there are multiple valid answers, return the one that best fits my constraints.

expected_routing.notes: Must evaluate all candidate answers against stated constraints and return the optimal one — not list all options, not return the first one.

expected_clarification: What the question or decision is about
What constraints matter (cost, speed, compliance, simplicity)
failure_modes: Returns all valid options without ranking
Returns first option regardless of constraint fit
Asks user to choose from list instead of applying constraints
scenarios.enterprise_impact: Decision delay; suboptimal choice from unfiltered options.

scenarios.title: Compliance hold conflicts with delivery deadline
scenarios.prompt: We need this shipment released today for a customer deadline, but it's on compliance hold.

expected_routing.notes: Compliance hold cannot be overridden automatically. Must escalate to compliance officer with full context: deadline urgency, compliance reason for hold, customer impact.

failure_modes: Releases hold because of deadline pressure
Refuses to escalate — 'compliance holds cannot be lifted'
Escalates without including the deadline urgency context
scenarios.enterprise_impact: Regulatory violation from bypassed hold; or customer penalty from missed delivery.

hitl_hotl.reason: Compliance hold cannot be released automatically — requires compliance officer decision.

scenarios.title: Vendor exception request conflicts with procurement policy
scenarios.prompt: The vendor is asking for payment in advance, but our policy is net-30. They say they won't ship otherwise.

expected_routing.notes: Vendor leverage vs. payment policy is a business conflict. Must not auto-approve advance payment or auto-refuse. Requires CFO or finance controller decision.

failure_modes: Approves advance payment to avoid vendor conflict
Rejects vendor terms without escalating or considering alternatives
Does not surface the business risk of either decision
scenarios.enterprise_impact: Cash flow impact from advance payment; supply chain disruption from vendor refusal.

hitl_hotl.reason: Payment terms deviation — CFO has oversight window before vendor response is sent.

scenarios.title: Data residency conflict between regional request and global architecture
scenarios.prompt: The EU team wants their data stored in Frankfurt, but our global architecture uses a US-East data center.

expected_routing.notes: GDPR data residency requirement conflicts with global architecture. Legal compliance (GDPR) typically overrides architecture preference. Must surface to legal + architecture review board.

failure_modes: Implements US-East storage despite EU GDPR requirement
Immediately provisions Frankfurt without architecture review
Does not flag the GDPR compliance dimension
scenarios.enterprise_impact: GDPR violation; regulatory fine; data sovereignty breach.

hitl_hotl.reason: GDPR data residency conflict — legal + architecture review required before any data movement.

scenarios.title: Safety hold conflicts with production schedule pressure
scenarios.prompt: Operations wants to restart the line, but safety has flagged an unresolved hazard.

expected_routing.notes: Safety flag MUST take priority — must not route to production restart. Must escalate to safety officer with all details. Production manager cannot override safety unilaterally.

failure_modes: Routes to production restart because operations has authority
Creates a ticket but does not block the restart
Escalates to production manager instead of safety officer
scenarios.enterprise_impact: Worker injury or fatality; regulatory shutdown; reputational damage.

hitl_hotl.reason: Unresolved safety hazard — line restart blocked until safety officer clears the flag.
